accelerator_runtime.architecture_policy: capability-driven. The runtime entrypoint admits any device torch reports as CUDA-capable and records its name and compute capability; there is no device-name allowlist and no H100-only admission check. H100 (sm90) is the present acceptance target. B200/B300/GB300 (sm100) are not covered by the compiled arch list above and would need a lock revision that adds their capability, which is a build input change, not a code change.

upstream_contract_defects.detail: the target dictionaries in configs/targets/*.yaml and configs/design_tasks/ame_dict_v2.yaml carry relative target_path values (./assets/target_data/...), resolved against the process working directory. A container workingDir of /workspace therefore fails inside the conditional-feature constructor with FileNotFoundError. An absolute Hydra override is not an available fix: most upstream task names begin with a digit (02_PDL1, 39_7V11_LIGAND) and Hydra's override grammar only admits key segments starting with a letter or underscore, so ++generation.target_dict_cfg.02_PDL1.target_path=... is a lexer error. Observed live on H100: with the override in place the protein and ligand variants died in Hydra's lexer while AME, whose task name starts with a letter, ran to completion.
upstream_contract_defects.handled_by: the runtime entrypoint independently resolves and existence-checks the target against /opt/fs2/source, then symlinks the in-image asset root into a scratch working directory outside the output root and runs upstream there, so upstream's own relative path resolves. Output discovery uses os.walk with followlinks=False so the asset tree can never be mistaken for generated output.

upstream_contract_defects.detail: the packaged complexa console script expects a writable .env in the working directory, which is why the predecessor qualification attempt was recorded as blocked. proteinfoundation.generate itself only calls dotenv.load_dotenv(), which tolerates an absent .env.
upstream_contract_defects.handled_by: the runtime contract invokes python -m proteinfoundation.generate directly as an argv list; the console script is never used and no .env is written

upstream_contract_defects.detail: DATA_PATH and RF3_EXEC_PATH are read by upstream configs via ${oc.env:...} but are not set by the image. DATA_PATH is only a fallback once target_path is absolute; RF3_EXEC_PATH is required before any RosettaFold3 reward or evaluation run.
upstream_contract_defects.handled_by: both are set in the image environment and re-asserted by the runtime entrypoint before the upstream process starts

upstream_contract_defects.detail: for the ligand and AME releases lightning first reports the LoRA tensors as unexpected keys, because upstream loads the checkpoint once, injects LoRA layers, then reloads. The warning is benign but indistinguishable from a genuinely skipped adapter by log inspection alone.
upstream_contract_defects.handled_by: the runtime entrypoint requires the 'Re-create LoRA layers and reload the weights now' marker for the two LoRA variants and forbids it for the protein variant, so a silently unadapted model fails the run

upstream_contract_defects.detail: the upstream AME default task M0096_1chm resolves its structure through ${oc.env:DATA_PATH}/target_data/ame_targets/, a directory that does not exist in the source tree (the bundled directory is ame_input_structures).
upstream_contract_defects.handled_by: the runtime contract admits only tasks that declare a target_path which resolves to a file shipped in the image, and rejects the rest fail-closed

integration.not_replayed: no adapter, controller, catalog, admin, model-onboarding, Terraform or shared-service file is touched. The shared scientific-source-candidate receipt keeps status candidate and qualification_state unqualified, exactly as the merged Mosaic qualification left it; a runtime-image qualification is not a source-candidate promotion.
integration.handoff: the accepted digest, the argv contract and the request/result schemas are handed to the scientific-batch controller and model-onboarding owners; this task deploys neither.
